definitions.explanation: Small pictorial symbols used in digital communication to express emotions, objects, or ideas. Originated in Japanese mobile phone culture in the late 1990s and became a worldwide standard.

⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦アプリ→アプリ：04722_apuri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{絵文字|えもじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{追加|ついか}→追加：04060_tsuika⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{絵|え}→絵：02613_e⟧ (picture) + ⟦{文字|もじ}→文字：03632_moji⟧ (character). The word was coined in Japan for pictographic characters used on mobile phones in the late 1990s. It has since been borrowed into English and many other languages as "emoji."

USAGE:
In Japanese, {絵文字|えもじ} can refer both to modern digital emoji and to older pictographic writing systems. In everyday use, it almost always means the digital kind. The related term ⟦{顔文字|かおもじ}→顔文字：21199_kaomoji⟧ refers to text-based emoticons like (^_^), which are distinct from {絵文字|えもじ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {絵文字|えもじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: use emoji
- {絵文字|えもじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: insert emoji
- {絵文字|えもじ}⟦{入力|にゅうりょく}→入力：04769_nyuuryoku⟧: emoji input
- ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{絵文字|えもじ}: new emoji
